hero.description1: Nano is the only currency with zero fees, sub-second finality, and no smart-contract complexity — purpose-built for the machine economy where AI agents transact autonomously.

instantSettlement.feelessText: Send $0.000001 economically. Every micro-payment is viable — perfect for per-token LLM billing, streaming compute costs, and pay-per-tool usage.
instantSettlement.decentralizedText: No central authority can freeze funds or censor transactions. Agents operate with full financial autonomy, guaranteed by decentralized consensus.

q1.question: Is Nano really feeless?
q1.answer: Yes. There are no transaction fees of any kind. Nano uses a lightweight, client-side proof of work to rate-limit spam — but this costs the sender nothing. Every raw unit you send is exactly what the recipient receives.

q2.question: How fast is Nano?
q2.answer: Typical transactions confirm in under 1 second. Nano's block-lattice architecture and Open Representative Voting (ORV) consensus eliminate the need for mining or block intervals, allowing near-instant finality.

q3.question: What is x402?
q3.answer: x402 is a protocol built on the HTTP 402 "Payment Required" status code. When an AI agent requests a paid resource, the server responds with payment details. The agent sends Nano, retries the request with proof of payment, and receives the resource — all without human intervention.

q4.question: Is Nano decentralized?
q4.answer: Yes. Nano uses Open Representative Voting (ORV) where account holders delegate voting weight to representatives of their choice. Anyone can run a representative node, and no single entity controls the network. Voting weight is distributed across hundreds of independent representatives.

q5.question: How do I start building with Nano?
q5.answer: Visit <link>docs.nano.org</link> for the protocol specification and RPC reference. You can run your own Nano node, use public RPC endpoints, or integrate via Nano MCP servers for AI agent workflows. Client libraries are available for Python, JavaScript, Rust, and more.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: NanoMarketCap ("we", "us", or "our") is committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, and safeguard information when you visit our website.

dataCollected.title: 1. Information We Collect
dataCollected.description: We collect minimal data necessary to operate the service:

ipAddresses.title: IP Addresses (Server‑Side, Ephemeral)
ipAddresses.description: We temporarily process your IP address for rate limiting (max 60 requests/minute per IP). This data is held in server memory only, never written to disk or a database, and is automatically purged every 5 minutes. IP addresses are extracted from the x-forwarded-for or x-real-ip request headers.

localStorage.title: Local Storage Preferences (Client‑Side)
localStorage.description: We store the following user preferences in your browser's local storage to remember your display settings across sessions:

items.parityFiat: Parity page fiat selection (default: USD, EUR)

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.description: We do not set any tracking or advertising cookies. The following functional cookies may be set automatically by our technology stack:

items.locale: NEXT_LOCALE — Stores your language preference for the site
items.theme: Theme preference — Remembers your light/dark mode selection

noTracking.title: 2. What We Do NOT Collect
noTracking.description: We do not use any analytics, tracking, or advertising services. There is no Google Analytics, no Facebook Pixel, no fingerprinting, and no behavioral profiling. We do not collect personal information such as names, email addresses, or payment details through the website.

thirdParty.title: 3. Third‑Party Services
thirdParty.description: We integrate with the following third-party services, each of which has its own privacy policy:

coingecko.title: CoinGecko API
coingecko.description: Market data is fetched server-side using our API key. No user data is transmitted to CoinGecko.

nanswap.title: Nanswap
nanswap.description: The swap page embeds a Nanswap iframe. When you interact with the Nanswap widget, your data (swap amounts, wallet addresses) is processed directly by Nanswap under their privacy policy. Our integration includes an affiliate referral identifier.

fonts.title: Fonts (Self‑Hosted)
fonts.description: Fonts are self-hosted at build time via Next.js font optimization. No runtime connections are made to Google servers and no user data is transmitted to Google.

imageCdns.title: Image CDNs
imageCdns.description: Cryptocurrency logos and images are loaded from CoinGecko and Nanswap CDNs, which may log standard web request data.

legalBasis.title: 4. Legal Basis for Processing (GDPR)
legalBasis.description: Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), our legal bases for processing data are:

items.legitimateInterest: Legitimate interest — Rate limiting to protect our service from abuse (IP address processing)
items.functionalCookies: Strictly necessary — Functional cookies (language, theme) are required for the website to operate as expected and are exempt from consent under the ePrivacy Directive
items.consent: Consent — Your browser preferences stored in local storage are never transmitted to our servers. The Nanswap swap widget is loaded only after your explicit consent

dataRights.title: 5. Your Rights
dataRights.description: Under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR), you have the right to:

items.access: Access — Request information about data we process about you
items.rectification: Rectification — Request correction of inaccurate data we hold about you
items.erasure: Erasure — Request deletion of any data we hold about you
items.restriction: Restriction — Request that we limit how we process your data
items.portability: Portability — Receive your data in a portable format
items.objection: Objection — Object to data processing based on legitimate interest
items.withdrawConsent: Withdraw consent — You may withdraw consent at any time by clearing your browser cookies and local storage

dataRights.note: Since we collect minimal data (ephemeral IP processing and browser-side preferences), most of these rights are satisfied by default. You can clear all locally stored preferences at any time through your browser settings.

supervisoryAuthority.title: 6. Right to Lodge a Complaint
supervisoryAuthority.description: You have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority, in particular in the EU Member State of your habitual residence, place of work, or place of the alleged infringement.
supervisoryAuthority.cnil: In France, the supervisory authority is the CNIL (Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés).
supervisoryAuthority.note: You may also contact your local data protection authority if you are located in another EU/EEA country.

dataBreach.title: 7. Data Breach Notification
dataBreach.description: In the event of a personal data breach that poses a risk to your rights and freedoms, we will notify the relevant supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, as required by GDPR Article 33. If the breach is likely to result in a high risk to your rights and freedoms, we will also notify affected individuals without undue delay.

internationalTransfers.title: 8. International Data Transfers
internationalTransfers.description: Our website is hosted by Vercel Inc. (United States). Server-side API calls are made to CoinGecko (global CDN). These transfers are conducted in accordance with applicable data protection regulations, including the EU–US Data Privacy Framework where applicable. We only transfer data that is strictly necessary for the operation of the service (ephemeral IP addresses for rate limiting). No personal data is stored outside the EU beyond transient server processing.

dataRetention.description: IP rate-limiting data: Automatically purged every 5 minutes from server memory. Local storage data: Persists in your browser until you clear it. We do not maintain any user database or persistent data storage.

cookies.intro: This policy explains how NanoMarketCap uses cookies, local storage, and similar browser technologies.

whatAreCookies.description: Cookies are small text files stored by your browser. Local storage is a browser feature that allows websites to store data locally on your device. Both are used to remember preferences and improve your experience.

functional.description: These cookies are necessary for the website to function properly:

manage.title: 5. Managing Your Preferences
manage.description: You can control cookies and local storage through your browser settings:

items.clearCookies: Clear cookies — Most browsers allow you to delete cookies through Settings → Privacy → Clear browsing data
items.clearStorage: Clear local storage — Open your browser's developer tools (F12) → Application tab → Local Storage → Clear
items.blockCookies: Block cookies — You can configure your browser to block all or specific cookies, though this may affect site functionality

retention.title: 6. Retention Periods
retention.description: Functional cookies persist until you clear them or they expire. Local storage data persists until you clear it manually. We do not set any expiration on local storage items — they remain until removed by you or your browser.
